ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier circuit. The inverting terminal is grounded through R1 and is fed back from the output terminal through R3, therefore forming a non-inverting amplifier form, and the closed-loop gain can be set by R1 and R3. uo is marked on the right side of the output terminal. The non-inverting terminal is connected through R2 to the resonant/coupling network at the lower left; the output terminal is also connected into this network through a series capacitor C2. At the lower left, two coupled inductors L1 and L2 with same-name terminal marks can be seen, among which L2 and capacitor C1 form a resonant branch, and the L1 side then returns through R2 to the '+' input terminal of the op amp. Reasoning: According to Barkhausen condition analysis, the loop can be opened at the op amp input terminal or output terminal to examine loop gain and phase. The op amp itself works as a non-inverting amplifier, the output is not inverted relative to the '+' input, and the amplification factor is approximately 1 + R3/R1. The feedback network is composed of C2, coupled inductors L1/L2, C1, and R2, etc., and can produce frequency-selective feedback near the LC resonant frequency. By selecting the values of L1, L2, C1, C2 and the same-name terminal polarity of the coupled inductors, the feedback voltage returning through the resonant network to the '+' input terminal can be made in phase with the output voltage, satisfying the loop phase condition; then making R3/R1 sufficiently large causes the op amp closed-loop gain to compensate for the losses of R2 and the resonant loop, so the loop gain can reach or exceed 1. Therefore, under appropriate parameter settings, this circuit satisfies the phase condition and amplitude condition for self-excited oscillation.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit structure in the image: an ideal op-amp non-inverting amplifier with gain set by R1 and R3, and a resonant feedback path from the output through C2 and the coupled L2/L1-C1 network back through R2 to the non-inverting input. Then break the loop at the op-amp input or output and apply Barkhausen analysis. At the LC resonance, choose L1, L2, C1, C2 and the coupling polarity so that the feedback voltage arriving at the '+' input is in phase with the output. Then choose R3/R1 large enough so that the op-amp gain compensates the losses/loading of R2 and the tank, giving loop gain >= 1. Since both Barkhausen phase and gain conditions can be met by parameter adjustment, conclude that the circuit can produce self-excited oscillation.
